newsitem.title: USA: Analysis finds Conrail vote will be close.
newsitem.headline: Analysis finds Conrail vote will be close.

text.p: A vote of Conrail Inc shareholders that is considered crucial to the railroad's proposed merger with CSX Corp is likely to be a close tally and will be determined by institutional investors, according to an analysis made by proxy firm Georgeson & Co.
The firm, hired by rival bidder Norfolk Southern Corp, also has determined that arbitragers hold about 20 percent of Conrail's stock, said Alan Miller, senior managing director at Georgeson.
Miller was testifying in the second day of a U.S. District Court hearing into the proposed transaction.
Norfolk Southern has filed suit to block the merger, which originally was proposed last month. A decision on the action is expected later Tuesday.

Miller said an initial analysis conducted by Georgeson determined that shareholders would overwhelmingly defeat a proposal to permit CSX to buy 40 percent of Conrail shares in a tender offer. Pennsylvania corporate law prohibits a company from buying more than 20 percent.
But the assessment changed after CSX and Conrail amended the terms of their agreement to provide shareholders with more cash in the transaction, Miller said.
"Our judgment is that at that point, the result is very close and is a function of a small change in how the institutions will vote," Miller said.
Shareholders are expected to vote in mid-December.

CSX is proposing to buy Conrail in an $8.5 billion cash and stock transaction that values Conrail shares at about $93 each. The terms call for CSX to pay $110 cash per share for 40 percent of Conrail's shares and exchange the rest for CSX stock. Norfolk Southern has offered $10 billion in cash for Conrail, or $110 per share.
Conrail has rejected the Norfolk Southern offer, contending that the CSX transaction would provide more strategic benefits.
